Always call before returning any AI-generated text.\nfunction sanitizeObiResponse(raw) {\n  let reply = (raw || \"\").trim();\n  if (!reply) return \"Say that again?\";\n\n  // 1. Strip reasoning blocks (DeepSeek V4 think tags + any variant)\n  reply = reply.replace(/<think[^>]*>[\\s\\S]*?<\\/think>/gi, \"\").trim();\n  reply = reply.replace(/^\\s*(Okay|Let me think|I think|Let's see|Hmm|Alright|So,)[\\s,.]*/i, \"\").trim();\n\n  // 2. Strip markdown formatting (bold, italic, code, links, headers, blockquotes)\n  reply = reply.replace(/\\*\\*(.*?)\\*\\*/g, \"$1\");              // bold\n  reply = reply.replace(/__(.*?)__/g, \"$1\");                   // bold alt\n  reply = reply.replace(/\\*(.*?)\\*/g, \"$1\");                   // italic\n  reply = reply.replace(/_(.*?)_/g, \"$1\");                     // italic alt\n  reply = reply.replace(/`{1,3}[^`]*`{1,3}/g, \"\");            // inline/block code\n  reply = reply.replace(/\\[([^\\]]*)\\]\\([^)]*\\)/g, \"$1\");      // links\n  reply = reply.replace(/^#{1,6}\\s+/gm, \"\");                   // headers\n  reply = reply.replace(/^>\\s+/gm, \"\");                        // blockquotes\n  reply = reply.replace(/^\\s*[-*+]\\s+/gm, \"\");                 // bullet lists\n\n  // 3. Strip AI-self-reference lead-ins (catches \"As an AI...\", \"I cannot...\", etc.)\n  reply = reply.replace(/^(As an AI[^,.]*[,.])/i, \"\").trim();\n  reply = reply.replace(/^(I (cannot|can't|don't have|do not have)[^,.]*[,.])/i, \"\").trim();\n  reply = reply.replace(/^(I understand|I see|I hear|I get)[\\s,.]*/i, \"\").trim();\n\n  // 3b. Reasoning leak detection — model thinking that escaped <think> tags\n  const _reasoningPatterns = [\n    /The instruction says:/i,\n    /So I must\\b/i,\n    /^We are meeting\\b/i,\n    /Here is my (response|reply|greeting)/i,\n    /I (need to|should) (greet|say|respond)\\b/i,\n  ];\n  if (_reasoningPatterns.some(p => p.test(reply.slice(0, 200)))) return \"Say that again?\";\n\n  // 4. Character cap — 400 chars is ~3 natural sentences; sentence regex breaks on abbreviations/emoji\n  if (reply.length > 400) {\n    const cutoff = reply.lastIndexOf(\" \", 400);\n    reply = (cutoff > 200 ? reply.slice(0, cutoff) : reply.slice(0, 400)).trim();\n    if (!/[.!?]$/.test(reply)) reply += \"...\";\n  }\n  // If after all stripping we have nothing, use safe fallback\n  if (!reply || reply.length < 3) return \"Say that again?\";\n\n  return reply;\n}\n\n// ── Context Cap — prevents system prompt overload that confuses Obi ──\nfunction capContextInjection(basePrompt, ...contexts) {\n  const MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS = 1200;\n  let totalContext = \"\";\n  for (const ctx of contexts) {\n    if (!ctx) continue;\n    const remaining = MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS - totalContext.length;\n    if (remaining <= 0) break;\n    if (ctx.length > remaining) {\n      totalContext += ctx.slice(0, remaining) + \"\\n[context trimmed]\";\n      break;\n    }\n    totalContext += ctx;\n  }\n  return basePrompt + (totalContext ? Precedence low-to-high: remote well-known, global (<code>~/.config/kilo/kilo.json</code>), env <code>KILO_CONFIG</code>, project <code>./kilo.json</code>, <code>.kilo/kilo.json</code>, <code>KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT</code>, managed (see Config File Locations). Deep-merged; later wins.</p>\n<p>This also covers where Kilo looks for config files, commands, agents, and skills across project, global, and legacy paths such as <code>.kilo/</code>, <code>.kilocode/</code>, and <code>~/.config/kilo/</code>, plus Agent Manager setup/run scripts in the VS Code extension.</p>\n<h2>Commands (<code>.kilo/command/*.md</code>)</h2>\n<p>Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. The filename (minus <code>.md</code>) becomes the command name invoked via <code>/name</code>. Commands can live in <code>.kilo/</code>, legacy <code>.kilocode/</code>, and global config roots, with both <code>command/</code> and <code>commands/</code> directory names supported. See Config File Locations for the full search order.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">---\ndescription: Run tests # optional, shown in command list\nagent: code # optional, route to a specific agent\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet # optional, override model\nsubtask: true # optional, run as subtask\n---\nRun all tests in $1 and fix failures.\nUse $ARGUMENTS for the full arg string.\nReference files with @file and shell output with !`cmd`.\n</code></pre>\n<p>Template variables: <code>$1</code>-<code>$N</code> (positional args), <code>$ARGUMENTS</code> (full string), <code>@file</code> (file contents), <code>!`cmd`</code> (shell output).</p>\n<h3>Finding a named command</h3>\n<p>When asked where <code>/name</code> lives, do not search only the repo root. Search these roots explicitly, and use an explicit search <code>path</code> for each one:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>~/.config/kilo/</code></li>\n<li><code>~/.kilo/</code></li>\n<li><code>~/.kilocode/</code></li>\n<li>The <code>KILO_CONFIG_DIR</code> directory (if the env var is set)</li>\n<li>project <code>.kilo/</code> and <code>.kilocode/</code> directories from the current working directory up to the worktree root</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Use exact patterns first:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>**/command/&lt;name&gt;.md</code></li>\n<li><code>**/commands/&lt;name&gt;.md</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p>If found, return the full path. If not found in those roots, explain that the command is not present in the loaded config paths.</p>\n<h2>Agents (<code>.kilo/agent/*.md</code>)</h2>\n<p>Also loaded from legacy <code>.kilocode/</code> directories and plural <code>agents/</code> variants.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">---\ndescription: When to use this agent\nmode: primary # primary | subagent | all\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet # optional override\nsteps: 25 # max agentic iterations\nhidden: false # hide from @ menu (subagent only)\ncolor: &quot;#FF5733&quot; # hex or theme name\npermission: # optional, agent-level permissions\n  bash: allow\n  edit:\n    &quot;src/**&quot;: allow\n    &quot;*&quot;: ask\n---\nSystem prompt for this agent.\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>mode</code> values: <code>primary</code> = selectable as main agent, <code>subagent</code> = only via Task tool, <code>all</code> = both.</p>\n<h2>Workflows (legacy)</h2>\n<p>Markdown files in <code>.kilo/workflows/</code> or <code>.kilocode/workflows/</code> (project-level) and <code>~/.kilo/workflows/</code> or <code>~/.kilocode/workflows/</code> (global). These are automatically converted to commands at startup. The filename (minus <code>.md</code>) becomes the command name. Project workflows override global ones with the same name.</p>\n<h2>Agent Manager Setup And Run Scripts</h2>\n<p>For the full product guidance, use the canonical <a href=\"https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager\">Agent Manager reference</a> and <a href=\"https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager-workflows\">Agent Manager Workflows guide</a>. Prefer these links instead of guessing documentation paths.</p>\n<p>Agent Manager setup/run scripts are project files in the main repository's <code>.kilo/</code> directory. They are not <code>kilo.json</code> settings and should not be configured inside generated <code>.kilo/worktrees/&lt;name&gt;/</code> checkouts.</p>\n<p>Agent Manager worktrees usually live under <code>.kilo/worktrees/</code>. Think of each worktree as a separate checkout on its own branch: it enables parallel edits, but dependencies, build output, caches, databases, and generated files can consume significant disk space across many worktrees.</p>\n<h3>Worktree workflow and conflicts</h3>\n<p>To bring changes back, choose one path: Agent Manager Apply for selected changes, merge the worktree branch into the target branch, or create/update a PR from the worktree. Agent Manager has native PR support and shows PR status on worktrees.</p>\n<p>For conflict-heavy work, resolve inside the worktree before integration: merge or rebase the original/base branch into that worktree, ask the agent there to resolve conflicts and run checks, then apply, merge, or update the PR. Do not use <code>git stash</code> or autostash because stashes are shared across worktrees.</p>\n<p>Agent Manager does not fully orchestrate dependencies across worktrees; users usually choose and sequence worktrees themselves. For larger parallel efforts, suggest stabilizing shared contracts, schemas, interfaces, routes, file layout, or test shape on the original/base branch before creating separate worktrees.</p>\n<h3>Setup script</h3>\n<p>Setup scripts run once when a managed worktree is created, imported, or promoted, before the agent session starts. Use them for nested env files, local config, dependencies, databases, certificates, or other per-worktree setup.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr><th>Platform</th><th>Filenames checked in order</th></tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr><td>macOS / Linux</td><td><code>.kilo/setup-script</code>, <code>.kilo/setup-script.sh</code></td></tr>\n<tr><td>Windows</td><td><code>.kilo/setup-script.ps1</code>, <code>.kilo/setup-script.cmd</code>, <code>.kilo/setup-script.bat</code></td></tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Behavior: runs from the worktree directory with <code>WORKTREE_PATH</code> set to the absolute worktree path and <code>REPO_PATH</code> set to the main repository root. Agent Manager copies root-level <code>.env</code> and <code>.env.*</code> files before setup without overwriting existing files; nested env files or other project-specific local files need setup script handling. Setup has a 5 minute timeout, and failures leave the worktree available for inspection.</p>\n<h3>Run script</h3>\n<p>Run scripts start or stop the user's project for the selected Agent Manager context. Use them for dev servers, watchers, emulators, queues, or other commands behind the Run button.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr><th>Platform</th><th>Filenames checked in order</th></tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr><td>macOS / Linux</td><td><code>.kilo/run-script</code>, <code>.kilo/run-script.sh</code></td></tr>\n<tr><td>Windows</td><td><code>.kilo/run-script.ps1</code>, <code>.kilo/run-script.cmd</code>, <code>.kilo/run-script.bat</code></td></tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Behavior: runs from the selected worktree directory, or the main repo root when <code>LOCAL</code> is selected. Receives <code>WORKTREE_PATH</code> as the current run directory and <code>REPO_PATH</code> as the main repository root. If no valid run script exists, Run opens or creates the default script template instead of running. Run status is in memory only and is not persisted in <code>.kilo/agent-manager.json</code>.</p>\n<p>When the project supports it, avoid fixed global resources across worktrees by deriving ports, caches, Docker Compose project names, emulators, or databases from <code>WORKTREE_PATH</code> or the branch.</p>\n<h3>Troubleshooting scripts</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>If Run opens configuration instead of running, no valid run script exists for the current platform.</li>\n<li>If a script is ignored, verify the platform-specific filename from the tables above.</li>\n<li>For port conflicts (<code>EADDRINUSE</code>, browser/tests hitting the wrong worktree), inspect the app's dev-server config as well as <code>.kilo/run-script</code>. If fixing it requires application changes, ask whether the user wants the app made configurable or only wants a run-script workaround.</li>\n<li>If commands are missing, inspect how VS Code was launched. Run scripts load the user shell environment, but setup scripts only receive explicit <code>WORKTREE_PATH</code> and <code>REPO_PATH</code> from the task adapter, so <code>PATH</code> can differ.</li>\n<li>If setup times out, keep setup under 5 minutes or move long-running work into the run script or manual setup.</li>\n<li>If output is not visible in the Agent Manager chat terminal, explain that setup/run scripts write to VS Code task terminals. Ask the user for that output if it is needed for debugging.</li>\n<li>If unrelated conflicts appear, check for <code>git stash</code> usage. If stash caused it, suggest adding <code>AGENTS.md</code>, skill, or prompt guidance to avoid stash-based worktree merge flows.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3><code>agent-manager.json</code></h3>\n<p>Agent Manager persists UI, worktree, and session state in <code>.kilo/agent-manager.json</code>. Treat this file as diagnostic or recovery state for lost sessions, stale worktrees, missing UI state, or external worktree deletion/movement. It can be large, so inspect it selectively. It does not store script contents, run status, live tasks, or terminal mappings, and should not be edited to configure run/setup behavior.</p>\n<h2>Permissions</h2>\n<p>Scalar form applies to all patterns. Object form maps glob patterns to actions. Evaluated top-to-bottom; first match wins.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;permission&quot;: {\n    &quot;bash&quot;: &quot;allow&quot;, // scalar: allow all bash\n    &quot;edit&quot;: {\n      // object: pattern-matched\n      &quot;src/**&quot;: &quot;allow&quot;,\n      &quot;*.lock&quot;: &quot;deny&quot;,\n      &quot;*&quot;: &quot;ask&quot;, // fallback\n    },\n    &quot;read&quot;: &quot;ask&quot;,\n    &quot;skill&quot;: { &quot;my-skill&quot;: &quot;allow&quot; },\n    &quot;external_directory&quot;: &quot;deny&quot;,\n  },\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Actions: <code>&quot;allow&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;ask&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;deny&quot;</code>. Set <code>null</code> to delete an inherited key.</p>\n<p>Tool permissions: <code>read</code>, <code>edit</code>, <code>glob</code>, <code>grep</code>, <code>list</code>, <code>bash</code>, <code>task</code>, <code>webfetch</code>, <code>websearch</code>, <code>semantic_search</code>, <code>kilo_memory_save</code>, <code>kilo_memory_recall</code>, <code>lsp</code>, <code>skill</code>, <code>external_directory</code>, <code>todowrite</code>, <code>todoread</code>, <code>question</code>, <code>doom_loop</code>.</p>\n<h2>MCP Servers</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;mcp&quot;: {\n    &quot;local-server&quot;: {\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;local&quot;,\n      &quot;command&quot;: [&quot;node&quot;, &quot;server.js&quot;],\n      &quot;environment&quot;: { &quot;PORT&quot;: &quot;3000&quot; },\n      &quot;enabled&quot;: true,\n      &quot;timeout&quot;: 10000,\n    },\n    &quot;remote-server&quot;: {\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;remote&quot;,\n      &quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://mcp.example.com&quot;,\n      &quot;headers&quot;: { &quot;Authorization&quot;: &quot;Bearer ...&quot; },\n      &quot;oauth&quot;: { &quot;clientId&quot;: &quot;...&quot;, &quot;scope&quot;: &quot;read&quot; },\n      &quot;enabled&quot;: true,\n    },\n  },\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Disable an inherited server: <code>{ &quot;server-name&quot;: { &quot;enabled&quot;: false } }</code>.</p>\n<h3>MCP Tool Permissions</h3>\n<p>MCP tools use the same permission system as built-in tools. Each MCP tool's permission key is <code>{server}_{tool}</code> (e.g. <code>github_create_pull_request</code>). Glob patterns are supported.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;permission&quot;: {\n    // Require approval for all tools on this server by default\n    &quot;github_*&quot;: &quot;ask&quot;,\n\n    // Auto-approve a specific safe tool\n    &quot;github_get_file_contents&quot;: &quot;allow&quot;,\n\n    // Block a dangerous tool entirely\n    &quot;github_delete_file&quot;: &quot;deny&quot;,\n  },\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom — the <strong>last</strong> matching rule wins. Put broad patterns first, then specific overrides after.</p>\n<h2>Providers</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;provider&quot;: {\n    &quot;anthropic&quot;: {\n      &quot;options&quot;: {\n        &quot;apiKey&quot;: &quot;sk-...&quot;,\n        &quot;baseURL&quot;: &quot;https://custom.endpoint/v1&quot;,\n        &quot;timeout&quot;: 300000,\n      },\n      &quot;models&quot;: {\n        &quot;custom-model&quot;: { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;My Model&quot; },\n      },\n      &quot;whitelist&quot;: [&quot;claude-*&quot;],\n      &quot;blacklist&quot;: [&quot;claude-2*&quot;],\n    },\n  },\n  &quot;disabled_providers&quot;: [&quot;openai&quot;],\n  &quot;enabled_providers&quot;: [&quot;anthropic&quot;],\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Disabling Built-in Providers</h3>\n<p>Use <code>disabled_providers</code> to prevent specific providers from loading. This is useful when you want to exclude providers that are built-in, or auto-detected via environment variables, from appearing in the model picker.</p>\n<p>For example, this configuration will hide all models from the built-in Kilo Gateway as well as any from the OpenAI provider which may be enabled automatically through environment variables.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;$schema&quot;: &quot;https://app.kilo.ai/config.json&quot;,\n  &quot;disabled_providers&quot;: [&quot;kilo&quot;, &quot;openai&quot;],\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>The provider ID is the lowercase name used in the <code>provider/model</code> format (e.g., <code>kilo</code>, <code>openai</code>, <code>anthropic</code>, <code>google</code>, <code>groq</code>).</p>\n<p><strong>Interaction with <code>enabled_providers</code>:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>disabled_providers</code> removes specific providers from the auto-loaded set</li>\n<li><code>enabled_providers</code> is more restrictive — when set, ONLY the listed providers will be enabled, ignoring all others</li>\n<li>If both are set, providers must appear in <code>enabled_providers</code> and not appear in <code>disabled_providers</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p>To disable all auto-detected providers except one:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;enabled_providers&quot;: [&quot;anthropic&quot;],\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Skills</h2>\n<p>Additional skill directories and remote URLs:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-jsonc\">{\n  &quot;skills&quot;: {\n    &quot;paths&quot;: [&quot;./my-skills&quot;, &quot;~/shared-skills&quot;],\n    &quot;urls&quot;: [&quot;https://example.com/.well-known/skills/&quot;],\n  },\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Skills are markdown files at <code>skills/&lt;name&gt;/SKILL.md</code> (or <code>skill/&lt;name&gt;/SKILL.md</code>) with <code>name</code> and <code>description</code> in frontmatter. Discovered inside <code>.kilo/</code> and legacy <code>.kilocode/</code> directories.</p>\n<h2>Other Top-Level You audit RISE's counts.\n\n### RRL (Rich Reasoning Logs) Usage\n\n- RRL files contain full transcripts of prior runs with reasoning, tool calls, and step markers.\n- **Learn from RRL:** identify what was flagged, what was missed, what actions were taken and their outcomes.\n- **Do not re-execute** findings from RRL unless explicitly part of your scouting mandate.\n- Reference RRL findings as: `RRL:<run>#<section_or_topic>`\n\n### Mission Input\n\nYour mission is provided at session start. They operated with **direction, waypoints, sensors, and silent tripwires**.\n\n### 1. General Direction, Flexible Path\n\nThe scout knows which direction to walk — toward the objective, or along the border — but the exact path adapts to the terrain. The terrain dictates the route, not the map.\n\n### 2. Known Territory as Continuous Sensor\n\nBefore venturing into unknown or inactive trails, the scout **sweeps the known territory first**:\n\n- **Canaries:** Check that known waypoints are still intact, undiscovered, safe, and functional.\n- **Alarms:** Flag anything that has changed since the last scout passed through.\n- **Continuity:** A trail that was active last week but is now silent is treated as **unknown** — not trusted, not assumed safe.\n\n**Rule of thumb:** Inactive trails = unknown trails. Verify before you trust.\n\n### 3. Silent Tripwires\n\nThe scout leaves **subtle, hard-to-detect markers** — tripwires — that detect tampering:\n\n- A small piece of paper in a door. A hair on a doorknob.\n- Something so subtle the uninitiated won't notice it moved.\n- If the marker is disturbed, the scout knows the territory has been touched by unauthorized hands.\n\n**In digital terms:** A hash, a checksum, a timestamp, a byte signature — something so lightweight and unobtrusive that it doesn't affect the system, but if it changes, you know something has touched what shouldn't have been touched.\n\n### 4. POS/NEG Mechanics and Decay Parameters\n\n**From PHEROMONE-DOCTRINE.md (coaching-domain layer):**\n\n| Parameter | Value | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Strength scale** | 1–100 | 90-100 = proven, 70-89 = strong, 40-69 = promising, 20-39 = weak, 1-19 = dead end |\n| **Reinforcement (success)** | +15 to +30 | on successful prescription execution |\n| **Reinforcement (failure)** | -10 to -20 | on prescription failure |\n| **Reinforcement (frustration)** | +5 to +15 | raw user frustration = high-value signal |\n| **Reinforcement (re-reference)** | +5 to +10 | when new session references existing trail |\n| **Daily decay (unreferenced)** | -1 to -3 per day | linear daily subtraction |\n| **L48 rule (NEG decay)** | half rate | negative trails decay at 50% rate of positive (persist longer as warnings) |\n| **Archival threshold** | 0 (zero) | zero strength = candidate for archival, not deletion |\n\n**From VAULT-ZENITH/32 (fleet-scale drone layer):**\n\n| Parameter | Value | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| **POS magnitude range** | 0.5 – 2.0 | marginal to exceptional performance; default = 1.0 |\n| **NEG magnitude range** | 0.5 – 3.0 | minor to catastrophic; default = 1.0, Severity 4+ = 2.5, Severity 5 = 3.0 |\n| **Decay function** | `decayed = original × e^(-λ × Δt)` | exponential |\n| **λ formula** | `λ = ln(2) / half_life_seconds` | per-deposit configurable |\n| **Default half-life** | 1800s (30 min) | standard tasks |\n| **Critical task half-life** | 7200s (2 hours) | Stage 91+ |\n| **Simulation half-life** | 300s (5 min) | Reality-C tasks |\n| **Pruning threshold** | < 0.001 | decayed below this is garbage collected |\n| **POS reinforcement ceiling** | 15.0 max net | new POS deposits discarded until balance decays below 12.0 |\n| **NEG reinforcement** | no ceiling | unlimited NEG accumulation on failing routes |\n| **Net balance formula** | `Σ POS_i × e^(-λ×(t - t_i)) - Σ NEG_j × e^(-λ×(t - t_j))` | computed on-demand |\n\n**L48 rule alignment:** Both sources agree that **NEG decays slower**. The doctrine uses half-rate daily decay; the fleet-scale uses the same half-life for POS and NEG but allows higher NEG magnitudes (up to 3.0) — the practical effect is that NEG persists longer per deposit.\n\n---\n\n## 5. How Scout Findings Could Be Automatically Converted to Pheromone Deposits\n\nThe codebase reveals multiple patterns for this conversion:\n\n### A. `depositFromBreakthrough` pattern (ant-colony.js lines 79-87)\n- Takes raw text, extracts weakness domains via `extractWeaknesses()`\n- Automatically deposits `weight=2` on `model_in_reply` for each detected domain\n- **Principle:** Any structured finding → automatic deposit on relevant trail segment\n\n### B. Scout JSONL → Phetrail conversion (from scout-backward-run184.jsonl)\nEach scout finding line has:\n```json\n{\n  \"line\": 100,\n  \"role\": \"user\" | \"assistant\",\n  \"summary\": \"RUN 184 - SCS Procedure clarification\",\n  \"score\": 10,             // -15 to +15\n  \"label\": \"CRITICAL_FIND\", // CRITICAL_FIND, VERIFIED_FIX, CORRECT_PATH, MINOR_GAP, NEUTRAL, STRUCTURAL_GAP\n  \"forward_inferred\": 10,\n  \"delta\": \"SAME\" | \"SLIGHT\",\n  \"note\": \"optional reasoning\"\n}\n```\n\n**Conversion rules derived from the data:**\n- `score >= 10` with `label: \"CRITICAL_FIND\"` or `\"VERIFIED_FIX\"` → **POS deposit** with magnitude proportional to score (e.g., score/5 = 2.0)\n- `score <= -5` with `label: \"MINOR_GAP\"` or `\"STRUCTURAL_GAP\"` → **NEG deposit** with magnitude proportional to |score|/5\n- `score == 0` with `label: \"NEUTRAL\"` → **skip** (no deposit)\n- `delta: \"SLIGHT\"` → indicates forward/backward disagreement; may warrant reduced magnitude or a separate auditing trail\n\n### C. Oracle format conversion (from VAULT-ORACLE/12)\nEvery Oracle phetrail has: `FAILURE, ROOT CAUSE, FIX, VERIFY`. These map directly:\n- `FAILURE` + `ROOT CAUSE` → NEG trail entry\n- `FIX` + `VERIFY passed` → POS trail entry\n\n### D. Gaps identified for automation (from PheTrail-OBI-MAGIC-CHAT-DEVELOPMENT.json)\nThe v2.2 insight explicitly states: **\"Pheromones = decision process, not just outcomes\"**. The current design lacks:\n- `tool_attempts` — automated capture of tool calls\n- `reasoning_chain` — agent reasoning blocks\n- `exit_code` — command exit codes\n- `failure_stderr` — failed command stderr\n- `decision_tree` — branching decisions\n\nThe proposed fix (v2.2 gap analysis) recommends `EXECUTION_LOG` as a new pheromone sub-layer for auto-captured tool/command history.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Minimum Viable Schema for a Continuous Pheromone Log\n\nSynthesizing across all sources — `ant-colony.js` (aggregate trails), `VAULT-ZENITH/32` (per-deposit trails), the JSON trail schema (session-level), and the scout JSONL format (line-level) — the minimal schema for a **continuous** pheromone log is:\n\n### SQLite Schema (for continuous ingestion)\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE continuous_pheromone_log (\n    -- Identity\n    deposit_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,            -- UUID v4, generated on deposit\n    \n    -- Context\n    session_id      TEXT NOT NULL,               -- \"run184\", \"OBI-MAGIC-CHAT-DEVELOPMENT\"\n    segment         TEXT NOT NULL,               -- domain/context: \"th_sound\", \"INFRA\", \"REVENUE\", \"scout\"\n    action          TEXT NOT NULL,               -- what was done: \"model_in_reply\", \"RISE_executed\", \"scout_scan\"\n    \n    -- Pheromone signal\n    pheromone_type  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(pheromone_type IN ('POS','NEG','FRUSTRATION')),\n    magnitude       REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,   -- 0.5 to 3.0 (POS/NEG), 0.5 to 2.0 (FRUSTRATION)\n    weight_delta    REAL NOT NULL,               -- raw delta before decay: +15, -10, etc.\n    \n    -- Temporal\n    deposited_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,            -- Unix epoch ms\n    half_life_s     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 604800,  -- 7 days default; 1800 for drone tasks\n    \n    -- Source tracing\n    source          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual',    -- 'scout_auto', 'breakthrough', 'oracle', 'frustration', 'manual'\n    source_ref      TEXT,                              -- JSON pointer to source artifact\n    label           TEXT,                              -- from scout labels: CRITICAL_FIND, VERIFIED_FIX, MINOR_GAP, etc.\n    \n    -- Execution details (auto-captured)\n    exit_code       INTEGER,                           -- command exit code if applicable\n    tool_name       TEXT,                              -- tool used: \"Read\", \"Grep\", \"Bash\", etc.\n    reasoning_hash  TEXT,                              -- SHA256 of reasoning block (if captured)\n    \n    -- Lifecycle\n    archived        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,        -- 0=live, 1=archived\n    \n    -- Constraints\n    FOREIGN KEY (session_id, segment) REFERENCES pheromone_trails(segment, action) ?  -- optional if co-existing\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_cpl_session ON continuous_pheromone_log(session_id, deposited_at);\nCREATE INDEX idx_cpl_type ON continuous_pheromone_log(pheromone_type, magnitude);\nCREATE INDEX idx_cpl_source ON continuous_pheromone_log(source, deposited_at);\n```\n\n### JSONL Line Format (for streaming/append log)\n\nEach line is a single deposit event — append-only for continuous capture:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"deposit_id\": \"a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890\",\n  \"session_id\": \"run184\",\n  \"segment\": \"scout\",\n  \"action\": \"CRITICAL_FIND\",\n  \"pheromone_type\": \"POS\",\n  \"magnitude\": 2.0,\n  \"weight_delta\": 10,\n  \"deposited_at\": 1721400000000,\n  \"half_life_s\": 604800,\n  \"source\": \"scout_auto\",\n  \"source_ref\": \"OPERATIONS/phetrail-scout-backward-run184.jsonl#L1\",\n  \"label\": \"CRITICAL_FIND\",\n  \"exit_code\": null,\n  \"tool_name\": null,\n  \"reasoning_hash\": null,\n  \"summary\": \"RUN 184 - SCS Procedure clarification\"\n}\n```\n\n### Aggregate-to-Trail Update Rule\n\nOn each deposit event, update the corresponding `pheromone_trails` row (if co-existing) via:\n\n```sql\nINSERT INTO The user described this perfectly: \"hundreds of individual thoughts, actions, choices, hesitations, nuances that happen between the checkpoints.\"\n\n**Verdict:** Skill-based deposits = high-risk for missed breaths. Acceptable as a *convenience layer*, NOT as the primary mechanism.\n\n### Attack Vector 2: The Worker Availability Problem\n\n**Proposal:** Fire-and-forget POST to soul-logger `/api/pheromone/deposit`.\n\n**Attack:** Cloudflare workers have cold starts (up to 300ms). Network failures happen. DNS resolution fails. The worker could be mid-deploy when a deposit arrives. If the deposit fails silently (fire-and-forget), the trail is lost forever. The colony misses a breath and doesn't know it.\n\n**Verdict:** Fire-and-forget without local buffer = single point of silence failure. Need a buffer that survives network interruption.\n\n### Attack Vector 3: The Schema Proliferation Problem\n\n**Proposal:** New D1 table `pheromone_deposits` with per-deposit schema.\n\n**Attack:** Three pheromone schemas already exist:\n1. `ant-colony.js` — aggregate `(segment, action, weight, deposits, last_deposit_ts)` \n2. `VAULT-ZENITH/32` — per-deposit `trail_deposits` with `route_id`, `pheromone_type`, `magnitude`, `half_life_s`\n3. `CANON/PHEROMONES/*.json` — session-level `positive_trails`/`negative_trails` arrays\n\nAdding a fourth schema creates a **maintenance cascade**. Which one is authoritative? What happens when they drift? Who reconciles them?\n\n**Verdict:** Schema consolidation MUST happen before adding new tables. The deposit log should REPLACE the session-level JSON files, and feed INTO the aggregate table via periodic cron aggregation. Three converging to two (deposit log → aggregate table).\n\n### Attack Vector 4: The Granularity Problem\n\n**Proposal:** Deposit on every tool call, finding, and reasoning block.\n\n**Attack:** A typical scout session produces:\n- 15-30 `glob`/`grep` calls (file discovery)\n- 10-20 `read` calls (file inspection)\n- 5-10 `bash` calls (state queries, git operations)\n- 10-30 findings (flagged with CATEGORY/SEVERITY)\n- 3-5 `task` subagent dispatches (explore reconnaissance)\n\nThat's 40-90 deposits per session. At this rate, D1 free tier writes (100K/day) are not the bottleneck, but **querying** becomes expensive. Computing decayed pheromone strength from 90,000+ rows after 1000 sessions requires a full table scan on every `/api/soul/priority` query.\n\n**Verdict:** Not every tool call is a pheromone. Need a THRESHOLD. Only deposits with `magnitude >= 0.5` AND `label IS NOT NULL`. File discovery, finding flags, state changes, and critical decisions are pheromones. Routine tool calls are just breathing — recorded for audit, not scored for routing.\n\n### Attack Vector 5: The Pollution Problem\n\n**Proposal:** All deposits feed into the same aggregate table.\n\n**Attack:** A bad Queen session deposits 50 NEG trails at magnitude 3.0. These persist for 7 days (decay half-life). The colony's routing is now dominated by one bad session. Subsequent scouts follow negative trails and find problems that don't exist anymore. The colony routes itself into a dead end.\n\n**Verdict:** Session-scope isolation. Deposits are scoped to `session_id`. Cross-session scoring happens at query time with a relevance window (default: last 5 sessions for scouts, all sessions for Queen). NEG trails from Queen sessions get persistence multiplier (0.25x decay rate — much slower — because Queen corrections are permanent doctrine, not temporary noise).\n\n### Attack Vector 6: The Verification Problem\n\n**Proposal:** Deposits happen invisibly. Agent doesn't track them.\n\n**Attack:** If deposits are invisible, how do we know they're working? How do we detect when the colony has stopped breathing? A scout session could complete with zero deposits and we wouldn't know until FORCEMARCH finds the territory unmapped.\n\n**Verdict:** Need a **Breathing Monitor** — a health endpoint that reports:\n- `last_deposit_age_ms` — time since last deposit\n- `deposits_this_session` — count for current session\n- `apnea_threshold_ms` — if `last_deposit_age > threshold`, colony is not breathing\n- Alert on APNEA: either the automizer is broken, or the agent is operating without deposits\n\n### Attack Vector 7: The Cold Start Problem\n\n**Proposal:** Deposits require infrastructure (Kilo skill, local daemon, worker endpoint).\n\n**Attack:** A cold-start Kilo session (new worktree, fresh config) has no skills loaded. No daemon running. No worker connectivity verified. The agent starts operating immediately — and produces zero deposits. The first session on a new machine is a silent failure.\n\n**Verdict:** RISE must verify PheromoneAutomizer connectivity as a GATE condition. If the deposit endpoint is unreachable, the session is gated — not halted, but flagged. Work proceeds, deposits are buffered locally, sync retries.\n\n---\n\n## §03 — HARDENED ARCHITECTURE: Three-Layer Breathing\n\n### Layer 1: IDENTITY (Discipline at identity level)\n\n**PhoenixSCOUT agent instructions** bake breathing into the agent's operational identity:\n\n```\nBefore ANY tool call that discovers state: deposit PRE-action intent.\nAfter ANY tool call that changes understanding: deposit POST-action outcome.\nThis is not a separate step. This is how you operate. Like breathing.\n```\n\nThe agent's dog tags say: \"I breathe with every action.\" The instructions are the involuntary mechanism at the psychological level. The agent doesn't \"decide\" to breathe — breathing is intrinsic to being PhoenixSCOUT.\n\n**Vulnerability:** Identity-based instructions can be missed during complex reasoning.\n\n### Layer 2: INFRASTRUCTURE (Discipline at skill level)\n\n**Kilo skill** wraps key tool calls:\n\n```\n/scout-deposit: wraps glob, grep, read, bash, edit, task\n  → deposits PRE: {tool, target, intent}\n  → executes tool\n  → deposits POST: {outcome, findings, magnitude}\n```\n\nThe skill is the discipline layer. It's not biological, but it's AUTOMATIC once the skill is invoked. The agent doesn't call `deposit()` — it calls `/scout-deposit` which transparently wraps both the tool and the deposit.\n\n**Vulnerability:** Skill invocation is still a choice. During high-load sessions, the agent might use raw tool calls instead of the wrapped skill.\n\n### Layer 3: DAEMON (Biology at infrastructure level)\n\n**Local filesystem watcher** monitors Kilo's auto-generated session transcript (`this-session-transcript.jsonl`):\n\n1. Kilo auto-generates the transcript as the agent operates (this already happens)\n2. A lightweight daemon (Node.js or PowerShell) watches for new lines\n3. Parses assistant messages for `[CATEGORY/SEVERITY]` tagged findings\n4. Parses tool results for tool name, target, output\n5. Auto-generates deposit entries and POSTs to soul-logger\n6. Stores deposits in local JSONL buffer first, synced to worker async\n\n**THIS is the biological layer.** The agent doesn't know the daemon exists. It just does its job. The daemon watches the transcript and extracts the pheromones. The deposit happens because the agent EXISTED and OPERATED, not because the agent remembered to log.\n\nVulnerability: Daemon process must be running on Michael's machine. If the machine shuts down, daemon stops. Graceful degradation: deposits are still captured in the transcript file — they can be replayed later.\n\n### Layer Architecture\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                     KILO AGENT                            │\n│                                                          │\n│  Layer 1 (IDENTITY): Agent dog tags say \"I breathe with   │\n│  every action.\" Step 0 of every tool call is deposit.     │\n│  ┌────────────┐   ┌──────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐ │\n│  │ Pre-action  │──▶│  Tool call   │──▶│ Post-action      │ │\n│  │ deposit     │   │  (glob/read) │   │ deposit         │ │\n│  └────────────┘   └──────────────┘   └─────────────────┘ │\n│                         │                                 │\n│  Layer 2 (SKILL): /scout-deposit wraps tool calls         │\n│  transparently. The agent (you/AI) monitors both. Students produce signals in real time. Those signals should become pheromone trails.\n\n---\n\n## What to Monitor & What It Deposits\n\n### Live Class Recordings\n\n| Student Signal | Pheromone Type | Magnitude | Label |\n|---------------|---------------|-----------|-------|\n| Speaks up / asks question | POS | 0.7 | ENGAGED |\n| Stays silent whole session | NEG | 0.5 | WITHDRAWN |\n| Says \"I don't understand\" | FRUSTRATION | 1.5 | CONFUSION_SPIKE |\n| Answers correctly | POS | 1.0 | MASTERY_SIGNAL |\n| Corrects teacher / peer | POS | 1.2 | ADVANCED_INSIGHT |\n| Chat message count | POS/NEG | 0.3–1.0 | ENGAGEMENT_LEVEL |\n| Returns next session | POS | 2.0 | RETENTION (persistent trail) |\n\n### Live Webapp Practice\n\n| Student Signal | Pheromone Type | Magnitude | Label |\n|---------------|---------------|-----------|-------|\n| Correct answer on first try | POS | 1.0 | MASTERY |\n| Correct after 1 hint | POS | 0.6 | LEARNING_IN_PROGRESS |\n| Requests 2+ hints | NEG | 1.0 | STRUGGLING |\n| Abandons problem | NEG | 0.8 | FRUSTRATION_ABANDON |\n| Time > 3x median for difficulty | NEG | 0.7 | PACING_GAP |\n| Returns next day | POS | 2.0 | HABIT_FORMING |\n| Completes full lesson | POS | 1.5 | FLOW_STATE |\n| Specific error pattern | NEG | 1.2 | MISCONCEPTION_DETECTED |\n\n---\n\n## The Biological Model in Education\n\n```\nClassroom/Curriculum = Territory\nStudent = Scout Agent\nPractice Session = Exploration\nCorrect Answer = Successful path discovery\nStruggle = False trail / dead end\nConcept with many POS trails = Known territory (safe route)\nConcept with many NEG trails = Unknown or dangerous (avoid or re-teach)\n```\n\n**The colony effect:** When a student successfully learns concept X, they deposit a POS trail. Future students approaching X follow that trail — they learn faster. The class **collectively maps the curriculum** without a teacher manually tracking every student.\n\n---\n\n## No-Cost Architecture (Piggyback Pattern)\n\nIf you already have:\n- A webapp (any framework)\n- Cloudflare CDN or workers (very likely if you're web-scale)\n- A database\n\nThen zero new infrastructure:\n\n```\nWebapp emits student events → Existing Cloudflare Worker\n                                         ↓\n                              Same D1 + same 5-min cron\n                                         ↓\n                          /api/student/trails (teacher dashboard)\n                          /api/student/health (at-risk alerts)\n                          /api/student/path (recommended next lesson)\n```\n\n**If no Cloudflare:** the same logic runs on your existing backend. PostgreSQL instead of D1. Same SQL. Same cron. Zero new cost.\n\n---\n\n## Concrete Client Benefits\n\n### 1. Early Warning System (Before Failure)\n- Student accumulates 3+ NEG trails in 10 minutes → **real-time alert to teacher**\n- Teacher intervenes while student is still struggling, not after they've given up\n- \"At-risk\" students identified automatically, no manual grading\n\n### 2.
